newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England leaves key rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England leaves key rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of England left its key interest rate unchanged at 6.0 percent on Friday, implying Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke decided at Thursday's monetary meeting not to raise official British rates.

Analysts had expected Bank of England Governor Eddie George to request a 1/4 point rate rise to cool demand in the economy but they also predicted Clarke would reject the calls because of worries about the May 1 election.

Clarke's ruling Conservative Party is around 20 points behind the main opposition Labour Party in the opinion polls and analysts doubted Clarke would risk antagonising voters by increasing the cost of borrowing.
Moreover, Clarke has argued that the strength of sterling, which hit a 4-1/2 year high this week, would act as a brake on inflation and that there was as yet no need to increase interest rates.
He is also wary of the uneven shape of the current economic mini-boom. The service and consumer sector are experiencing strong demand but growth in manufacturing is sluggish.
The pound's strength is already pushing up the cost of British exports and is likely to cut demand further. Raising interest rates could make the pound even stronger.
